message:
feat(host): say which stage a preview spent its time in

Product 3. Instrumentation, and the measurement it exists to produce has NOT been taken -- see
below.

"549ms against a 400ms deadline" says the deadline held and nothing about where the other 149
went. The result now carries the three stages separately: spawn (mapping, event, CreateProcessW),
wait (the deadline itself), and teardown (TerminateProcess and confirming the process is actually
gone). It also carries helperLingering, which is the state where that confirmation did not come
and the next request will be refused.

On the result rather than in a test, so the host logs it in the field. A preview that stalls on
someone's machine should say which stage, and "the kill is instant" is an assumption this makes
falsifiable rather than one it keeps.

One bug was written and caught by reading it back rather than by running it. The teardown time was
first reported through a pointer into the local result object, written by Attempt's destructor --
which runs after the return value has been initialised. With NRVO that happens to land in the
caller's storage; without it, it writes into a local the return has already moved from. The caller
now owns the storage and passes a pointer down, which is correct either way.

What has not happened: a run. Producing the breakdown means executing the helper end-to-end suite,
which starts capture processes on this machine, and the user has asked about exactly that activity
-- I had been starting hosts and helpers repeatedly for the end-to-end work and did not say so
first. That is paused until they say how they want it handled, so the fields are populated by code
that compiles and by nothing that ran.

The four suites that touch none of this still pass: budget 45, wait 20, fetch policy 13, shipped
helper gate 16.
